title: Inverse image of sheaves of sets along an etale morphism is restriction
statement: Let $j:U\to X$ be an etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism], with small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; an object $V\to U$ of $U_{\Et}$ gives the object $V\to U\xrightarrow{j}X$ of $X_{\Et}$. For a sheaf of sets $G$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] let $G|_U(V\to U)=G(V\to X)$, with the restriction maps of $G$. Let $j^{-1}G$ and $j^*s\in(j^{-1}G)(W\times_XU)$ for $s\in G(W)$, $W$ in $X_{\Et}$, be the etale inverse image of sheaves of sets and the image of $s$ under its unit [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. Then: (1) $G|_U$ is a sheaf of sets on $U_{\Et}$ and there is an isomorphism of sheaves of sets $\rho_G:j^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}G|_U$, natural in $G$; (2) for every object $W$ of $X_{\Et}$ and $s\in G(W)$, $\rho_G(j^*s)=s|_{W\times_XU}\in G(W\times_XU)$, the restriction of $s$ along the projection $W\times_XU\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. In particular $\rho_G(U):(j^{-1}G)(U)\xrightarrow{\sim}G(U)$.

proof.text: Write $Y=U$, so $j:Y\to X$ and $G|_Y=G|_U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-localization-functor-adjoint] the functor $\iota_j:Y_{\Et}\to X_{\Et}$ sending $V\to Y$ to $V\to X$ is well-defined, and the base-change functor $b_j:X_{\Et}\to Y_{\Et}$ sends $W$ to $W\times_XY$. The adjunction $\iota_j\dashv b_j$ has counit the projection $p_W:W\times_XY\to W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] the direct image on sheaves of sets is $(j_*F)(W)=F(W\times_XY)$, i.e. precomposition with $b_j$.

Precomposition with $\iota_j$ preserves sheaves: a covering of an object of $Y_{\Et}$ remains a jointly surjective etale covering after viewing all maps over $X$, and fibre products are unchanged. Precomposition with $b_j$ preserves sheaves because [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] makes the base-changed family a covering and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] identifies the base-changed fibre products. Therefore $G|_Y=G\circ\iota_j$ is a sheaf of sets and $j_*F=F\circ b_j$ is a sheaf of sets.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sets-adjoint-continuous-restriction-adjunction] to $\lambda=\iota_j$ and $\beta=b_j$. It gives an adjunction from sheaves of sets on $X_{\Et}$ to sheaves of sets on $Y_{\Et}$, with unit $u_G(W)=G(p_W):G(W)\to G(W\times_XY)$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction], the sheafified inverse image along the base-change functor is left adjoint to precomposition with that functor; by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] this is the set-valued inverse image $j^{-1}$ and direct image $j_*$, and $\eta_{j,G}:G\to j_*j^{-1}G$, $s\mapsto j^*s$, is its unit. The functor $b_j$ satisfies the hypothesis by Step 2. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-adjoint-continuous-restriction-adjunction] therefore gives a unique natural isomorphism $\rho:j^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(-)|_Y$ such that $j_*(\rho_G)\circ\eta_{j,G}=u_G$. This proves clause (1), including naturality.

Evaluate $j_*(\rho_G)\circ\eta_{j,G}=u_G$ at $W\in X_{\Et}$. Since $(j_*\rho_G)(W)=\rho_G(W\times_XY)$ and $u_G(W)=G(p_W)$, this is exactly $\rho_G(W\times_XY)\circ\eta_{j,G}(W)=s|_{W\times_XY}$ for $s\in G(W)$. Taking $W=X$ and identifying $X\times_XY$ with $Y$ gives the global-sections assertion; $\rho_G(Y)$ is an isomorphism as a component of $\rho$.
